title: Derived direct image and evaluation of coefficient systems
statement:
Let $u:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a geometric morphism of topoi presented by small sites, meaning an adjoint pair $u^*\dashv u_*$ on sheaves with $u^*$ preserving finite limits. Let $O$ be a commutative ring, let $\lambda\in O$ be a non-zero-divisor, assume $O\cong\varprojlim_{n\geq1}O/(\lambda^n)$, and put $A_n=O/(\lambda^n)$. For either topos $\mathcal T$, let $\mathsf S_A(\mathcal T)$ be the abelian category whose objects are strict systems of sheaves of modules $M_n$ over the constant ring sheaf $(A_n)_{\mathcal T}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and transition maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}M_n$ linear along $A_{n+1}\to A_n$, and whose morphisms are compatible families of module maps. Restriction of scalars has its usual meaning [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Equivalently these are modules over the ring object $((A_n)_{\mathcal T})_n$ in the topos of inverse sequences. Exactness and the evaluation functors $e_n$ are levelwise. Use the unbounded derived categories of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with the standard cohomology of complexes.

Applying $u^*$ levelwise is exact and gives $u_A^*:D(\mathsf S_A(\mathcal Y))\to D(\mathsf S_A(\mathcal X))$. Levelwise $u_*$ has a total right derived functor $Ru_{A,*}$, computed by K-injective resolutions in the category of systems [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and $u_A^*\dashv Ru_{A,*}$. There are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$e_nRu_{A,*}\cong Ru_*e_n,\qquad e_nu_A^*\cong u^*e_n.$$
These comparisons intertwine the evaluated units and counits with the ordinary level adjunctions and are compatible with the quotient maps, on objects and on morphisms. Inverse image commutes with the derived changes of constant coefficient ring $-\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. A complex of systems is called normalized here if every adjoint transition $M_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\to M_n$ is an isomorphism for $m\geq n$.

Suppose additionally that for every $n$, $u^*:D^+(\mathcal Y,A_n)\to D^+(\mathcal X,A_n)$ is fully faithful, and let $M\in D^+(\mathsf S_A(\mathcal X))$ have all evaluations in its essential image. Then the counit $u_A^*Ru_{A,*}M\to M$ is an isomorphism of derived systems; $Ru_{A,*}M$ is bounded below, and if $M$ is normalized, so is $Ru_{A,*}M$. In particular this applies to the comparison $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for finite coefficient rings [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison].

source.place: Construction 4.1 (printed p. 21), Lemma 4.10 and its proof (printed pp. 23–24). Final origin/normalization clause is the formal consequence of evaluation, counit, exact inverse image and derived tensor compatibility stated here.

proof.text: Choose a small presenting site $\mathcal C$ for either topos. Present its sequence topos on $\mathcal C\times\mathbf N_{\geq1}$, with the usual order on the second factor and coverings generated by covers of $\mathcal C$ at a fixed index. A sheaf is precisely a sequence of sheaves: restriction along $q\leq r$ gives its map from level $r$ to level $q$. Put the ring $A_q$ at index $q$. Modules on this small ringed site are exactly the systems in the statement; checking the sheaf condition and module operations at each index gives the equivalence, including maps. Consequently [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] applies. Kernels and cokernels are componentwise, so evaluation is exact. The inverse image of a geometric morphism preserves the constant ring sheaves and is exact on their modules: it preserves kernels by finite limits, and cokernels by its colimit-preserving adjunction. The level module adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] respects the transition squares, hence gives $u_A^*\dashv u_{A,*}$ on systems. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] to the exact inverse images and evaluations. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] to the additive direct images, using the K-injective resolutions just obtained, and then [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] to obtain $u_A^*\dashv Ru_{A,*}$ and $u_n^*\dashv Ru_{n,*}$ on the unbounded categories.

source.place: Construction 4.1 and paragraph before Lemma 4.10; Stacks 07A5, 079P, 070K, 015F, 09T5 and 03D7 for the generic module/derived constructions

proof.text: Use $LE_n\dashv e_n$ and its strict tensor model from [lem-pur-coefficient-evaluation-derived-left-adjoint]. Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to N$ over $A_n$. The coefficient-$A_n$ inverse image sends $P$ to a flat-term K-flat complex by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat]. In the two strict system complexes $u_A^*E_nP$ and $E_n(u_n^*P)$ the components above $n$ are zero, and at $q\leq n$ the tensor comparison is $u^*(P\otimes_{A_n}A_q)\cong u^*P\otimes_{A_n}A_q$. These comparisons are the canonical pullback/tensor maps of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], with the second factor the constant quotient ring; they preserve its $A_q$ action. On local tensor generators the map carries $x\otimes a$ to the corresponding pulled-back generator $u^*x\otimes a$. Reducing $a$ to a lower quotient commutes with this formula. Thus the comparisons define an isomorphism of strict complexes of systems, natural in $P$ and its maps, and descend via the resolution model to $u_A^*LE_n^{\mathcal Y}\cong LE_n^{\mathcal X}u_n^*$. For the separate coefficient-change assertion, take a flat-term K-flat resolution $Q\to N$ over $A_m$. Pulling back $Q$ preserves these properties by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], and tensoring $Q$ with $A_n$ computes its derived scalar extension. Exact inverse image therefore represents the left-hand side by $u_n^*(Q\otimes_{A_m}A_n)$, and the right-hand side by $u_m^*Q\otimes_{A_m}A_n$. The natural degreewise pullback/tensor map identifies these complexes as $A_n$-complexes and commutes with their differentials and maps of resolutions. It induces $u_n^*(N\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n)\cong u_m^*N\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$ for every $m\geq n$; no flatness of $A_n$ over $A_m$ is used.

source.place: Construction 4.1 and the derived base-change isomorphism immediately before Lemma 4.10; Stacks 0G7E and 07A4

proof.text:
For $N\in D(\mathcal Y,A_n)$ and $M\in D(\mathsf S_A(\mathcal X))$, form the natural chain of bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(N,e_nRu_{A,*}M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(LE_n^{\mathcal Y}N,Ru_{A,*}M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(u_A^*LE_n^{\mathcal Y}N,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(LE_n^{\mathcal X}u_n^*N,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(u_n^*N,e_nM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(N,Ru_{n,*}e_nM).$$
The outer evaluation adjunctions are [lem-pur-coefficient-evaluation-derived-left-adjoint], the direct-image adjunctions were established in step 1 using [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors], and the middle isomorphism is step 2. The Yoneda bijection [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] turns this into a natural isomorphism $\beta_n:e_nRu_{A,*}\cong Ru_{n,*}e_n$. In particular this argument proves the unbounded comparison without asserting that evaluation preserves K-injectives in the varying-ring system category. The pullback comparison $e_nu_A^*\cong u_n^*e_n$ is already the termwise identity of step 1.

source.place: Lemma 4.10, equation (4.10.1), obtained by adjunction from the preceding displayed base-change isomorphism

proof.text:
Write $\eta^A,\varepsilon^A$ for the system adjunction and $\eta^n,\varepsilon^n$ for the level adjunction. The Hom chain defining $\beta_n$ sends the identity of $e_nRu_{A,*}M$ to the adjunct of $e_n\varepsilon^A_M$. Therefore
$$\varepsilon^n_{e_nM}\,u_n^*\beta_{n,M}=e_n\varepsilon^A_M.$$
Applying the same chain to the system unit, and using $\varepsilon^Au_A^*\circ u_A^*\eta^A=1$, gives
$$\beta_{n,u_A^*N}\,e_n\eta^A_N=\eta^n_{e_nN}.$$
These are the required evaluated counit and unit identities. For each quotient $A_m\to A_n$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] to the identity topos with this structural ring map: ordinary tensor extension is left adjoint to coefficient restriction. Restriction is exact since it leaves the underlying abelian sheaf unchanged. The left derived extension exists by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], so [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] gives $C_{mn}=-\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\dashv\operatorname{Res}_{A_m\to A_n}$ on the unbounded categories. To check quotient maps, use the maps $\sigma_{mn}:LE_nC_{mn}\to LE_m$ of [lem-pur-coefficient-evaluation-derived-left-adjoint]. Their precomposition action is exactly the adjoint transition of a system. Step 2 commutes with $\sigma_{mn}$: on a common K-flat complex its components below $n$ are the same tensor comparison on both routes, and above $n$ both maps have zero source. Hence the Hom chain in step 3 commutes with precomposition by $\sigma_{mn}$; its mates say precisely that $\beta_m,\beta_n$ respect $M_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{A_m\to A_n}M_n$. The canonical identification of coefficient restriction with derived pushforward along the identity ringed topos, followed by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], identifies $Ru_{m,*}\operatorname{Res}_{A_m\to A_n}$ with $\operatorname{Res}_{A_m\to A_n}Ru_{n,*}$. Thus both sides of the transition square have the required coefficient category. Naturality of every Hom bijection also gives these identities for morphisms of input derived systems. Identity and composition of quotient maps follow from those of $\sigma_{mn}$.

source.place: Lemma 4.10 and Construction 4.1, adjunction mates; Stacks 0D6E for restriction/direct-image composition

proof.text: Now take $M\in D^+(\mathsf S_A(\mathcal X))$ with a uniform lower cohomological bound $a$. Both system categories are Grothendieck by their small ringed-site presentation in step 1 [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The functor $u_{A,*}$ is left exact since it is a right adjoint. Its total derived functor restricted to bounded-below complexes agrees with the bounded-below construction: a bounded-below injective resolution is K-injective [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution], and hence computes that same total derived functor. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] to conclude $Ru_{A,*}M\in D^{\geq a}$, in particular it is bounded below. This supplies a bound for the system, rather than separate bounds depending on $n$.

source.place: Tag 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing), with 070K and the bounded-below injective resolution construction

proof.text: Assume the full-faithfulness and essential-image hypotheses. For a bounded-below $G\in D^+(\mathcal Y,A_n)$, full faithfulness identifies, for every bounded-below $H$, the map $\operatorname{Hom}(H,G)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H,Ru_{n,*}u_n^*G)$ induced by the unit with the bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(H,G)\to\operatorname{Hom}(u_n^*H,u_n^*G)$. All these objects are bounded below by step 5 at a single level. The Yoneda bijection [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] makes the unit an isomorphism. The triangle identity then makes the counit at $u_n^*G$ the inverse of $u_n^*\eta^n_G$. Since $e_nM$ is isomorphic to some $u_n^*G$, naturality makes its counit an isomorphism too. By step 4 and $\beta_n$, every evaluation of the system counit $\varepsilon^A_M$ is therefore an isomorphism. Evaluations jointly detect derived isomorphisms: the evaluated cone is acyclic at every $n$, so the cone has every cohomology system zero, because kernels and images are levelwise. Thus $u_A^*Ru_{A,*}M\to M$ is an isomorphism of derived systems [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Formal essential-image consequence of Lemma 4.10; definition of the derived category and its levelwise cohomology

proof.text:
Set $N=Ru_{A,*}M$ and assume $M$ normalized. For $m\geq n$, let $t_N:N_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\to N_n$ be its adjoint transition. The coefficient-square compatibility of step 4 and tensor comparison of step 2 give the equality
$$\varepsilon^n_{M_n}\,u_n^*t_N=t_M\bigl(\varepsilon^m_{M_m}\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\bigr),$$
with the pullback/tensor identification on the source understood, and with $u_n^*N_n\to M_n$, $u_m^*N_m\to M_m$ identified with the evaluated system counit by $\beta$. Here is the derived-morphism verification. Write $C_{mn}=-\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$ and $\varepsilon_q=e_q\varepsilon^A_M$. Naturality of the transition-adjoint map, equivalently the Hom-adjunction formula for $\sigma_{mn}$ in step 4, gives $\varepsilon_n\circ t_{u_A^*N}=t_M\circ C_{mn}(\varepsilon_m)$. The strict comparison of step 2 identifies $t_{u_A^*N}$ with $u_n^*t_N$ and identifies $C_{mn}(u_m^*N_m)$ with $u_n^*C_{mn}(N_m)$: on a flat-term K-flat representative the comparison commutes with the identity components of $\sigma_{mn}$ at $q\leq n$ and with its zero-source components at $q>n$. Substitute these identifications in the preceding naturality equation. This proves the displayed equality for derived morphisms without requiring the counit to be a map between the chosen K-flat resolutions. Both evaluated counits are isomorphisms by step 6, and $t_M$ is an isomorphism by normalization. Hence $u_n^*t_N$ is an isomorphism. Finally $u_n^*$ reflects isomorphisms on the whole unbounded derived category: it is exact, so $H^i(u_n^*K)=u_n^*H^i(K)$; full faithfulness on $D^+$ implies faithfulness on degree-zero module sheaves, so $u_n^*H=0$ forces $1_H=0$, and $H=0$. Apply this to every cohomology of the cone of $t_N$. Its pulled-back cone is zero, so every cohomology is zero and $t_N$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Therefore $N$ is normalized. This reasoning never assumes that $N_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$ is bounded below.

source.place: Formal normalization consequence of Lemma 4.10 and Construction 4.1; transition condition (4.12.2), called weak normalization in Definition 4.12; Stacks 07A4

proof.text: For $u=\nu_T$, the geometric morphism is the one in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. When every $A_n$ is finite, [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] states exactly the required full faithfulness of $\nu_T^*$ on $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A_n)$. Thus the conclusions just proved apply to bounded-below systems on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ whose evaluations are of etale origin, and to normalized ones among them.

split_report.summary: Proved the varying-ring system comparison by the derived left adjoint of evaluation and a natural Hom calculation. Added one statement-only derived evaluation-extension lemma, used existing small ringed-site K-injective and tensor tools, wrote the quotient and unit/counit identities, and proved bounded-below essential-image descent and normalization by conservative exact pullback. Statement unchanged.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the ancestor def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image adic-stage paragraph: coherent passage of the input system between sites before applying the compatible finite-level exceptional operations. No assertion of the exceptional adjoint itself is used or replaced.

tool_uses.why: Generic module adjunction on small ringed topoi, applied levelwise; this unit has no separate underived module-adjunction theorem.
Generic K-injective computation of total right derived functors on unbounded categories, not a replacement of the six-operation route.
Generic derived adjunction for everywhere-defined total derived functors, needed for both the system and level adjunctions.
Generic K-flat pullback preservation verifies the simultaneous tensor models; no varying-system result is taken from it.
Generic derived tensor compatibility supplies coefficient pullback on unbounded complexes; this unit does not replace its ringed-topos construction.
Generic derived composition identifies coefficient restriction followed by direct image with the reverse composite.
Generic bounded-below resolution theorem identifies the D+ restriction of the already-constructed total functor.
Generic uniform lower-bound theorem applied to the system category itself.
The existing finite-level etale/pro-etale full-faithfulness theorem discharges the final specialization; it is the comparison explicitly named by the item and its ancestor.

Generic exact-functor localization identifies the termwise exact inverse images and evaluations with their everywhere-defined left and right derived functors in step 1; this does not replace the coefficient-system comparison route.
